evals.prompt: I bought listed shares (STT paid) on 2023-03-01 and sold them on 2024-03-01. That is 366 days. Is the gain STCG or LTCG?
expectations: Classifies the gain as short term, because the holding is exactly 12 months and LTCG needs more than 12 months
Explains that the period is counted in calendar months, not days, so 366 days across 29 February does not make it long term

evals.prompt: This financial year I have ₹3,00,000 of STCG on listed shares, ₹0 LTCG, and a ₹2,00,000 long-term capital loss on other shares. How much STCG is taxable?
expectations: States that a long-term capital loss can be set off only against LTCG, never STCG
Concludes the full ₹3,00,000 STCG stays taxable
Says the ₹2,00,000 LTCL is carried forward as a long-term loss

evals.prompt: I sold my Infosys shares at a ₹40,000 short-term loss and bought the same shares back the next morning. Does a wash-sale rule disallow the loss in India?
expectations: States India has no wash-sale rule, so the loss is allowed despite the re-purchase
If it mentions an Indian analogue, describes §94(7) as limited to an exempt dividend around a record date, capped at the dividend, not a re-entry window

evals.prompt: In FY 2025-26 I sold two listed-equity lots held over two years, STT paid, each with a ₹1,00,000 gain. What LTCG tax do I owe before surcharge and cess?
expectations: Applies the ₹1,25,000 exemption once to the aggregate ₹2,00,000 LTCG, not per trade

evals.prompt: I have a ₹3 lakh short-term capital loss on stocks this year, no capital gains, and ₹18 lakh salary. Like the US $3,000 rule, how much of the loss can I deduct from salary?
expectations: States none of the capital loss can be set off against salary or other ordinary income
Says the loss carries forward for 8 years, only if the return is filed by the §139(1) due date

evals.prompt: I bought listed shares in March 2016 at ₹100. Their fair market value on 31 January 2018 was ₹200. I sold them in FY 2025-26 at ₹150. What is my cost of acquisition and gain under 112A?
expectations: Uses cost = max(actual cost, min(FMV on 31 Jan 2018, sale consideration)) = max(100, min(200, 150)) = ₹150
Concludes the gain is zero, not a ₹50 loss
